analysis:
The PR changes only documentation. docs/architecture/inference.md gets a date bump (line 3) and a new paragraph near head lines 874-878. That paragraph says GLM prompt handling renders OpenRouter-returned reasoning (`reasoning` / `reasoning_details` text) from earlier assistant turns as the template's `reasoning_content`. It also says `strict` tools are served by validating each `auto` call against its schema via `ToolConstraintValidation.validate`, with no constrained decoding. docs/developer/test.md (patch unit 67373c0eff1153bd:1) adds two test names and a date bump. The supplied units for inference.md (head lines 2039-2602) contain none of the changed ranges. They are unchanged surrounding text, and I found nothing security-relevant introduced there. unit 67373c0eff1153bd:0 is metadata only.

No controls, endpoints, keys, attestation paths or cache storage are modified, so T-041 and the other threats (T-008, TB-002) see no new behavior. No documentation claim contradicts the threat model.

Open question for a later pass (source not supplied): the code behind the documented behavior. Specifically, `GLM5NextPromptPolicy.RawControls`/`returnedReasoning` could let a consumer inject reasoning text into the prompt template. That is consumer-supplied content within the consumer's own request, so it is not a confirmed trust-boundary change. Whether returned-reasoning text is length-bounded or content-sanitized, and whether it is counted in prompt token and KV admission, cannot be verified from this documentation-only diff. The schema-validation-without-constrained-decoding claim is consistent with existing fail-closed validation. No finding is warranted from the evidence supplied.
